newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes off low but remains in downtrend.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes off low but remains in downtrend.

text.p: Fund selling on the opening of New York's Comex futures knocked silver prices lower but they pulled back most of their losses by Monday's afternoon gold fix.
None of the other metals in the precious complex was affected by silver which had been looking vulnerable since its last attempt to break higher failed on June 24.
"(cash) Silver got to a low bid of $4.62 but it found trade buying and looks fairly steady at $4.66/$4.68," a dealer said.
Gold might have been unaffected by silver's moves but it was still having trouble holding above $334.05 per ounce where it set its lowest fixing since March 30, 1993 this morning.
It fixed at 1400 GMT at $334.55 in a market which seemed to lack the will to make a move one way or the other.
The August Comex gold contract was indicated at $335.10 up $0.20 at the fixing.
"There is not much either way in gold. It seems to be trying to settle into a new range," one dealer said.
Views of that range were not bullish. Some dealers cited a $326-$334 bracket for the yellow metal but a further plunge to $315. Then the March 1985 low of $287.25 was the next target.
"I'm not bullish but it is a question of the timing for these levels," one dealer said.
He added that there was very little physical interest in market partially due to the close of the Hong Kong markets while the territory reverts to Chinese rule this week.
U.S. monetary policy advisory Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) holds a two-day meeting beginning July 1 after which U.S. interest rates are forecast to remain unchanged.
Another dealer said there was little to get bullish about in gold, citing the market showing many of the symptoms of being in the first phase of two-three year bear market.
"When you're in a market like that all you can do is sell the rallies," the dealer said.
Platinum and palladium moved in opposite direction with the former firming to $427.00/$431.00 up $11.00 and the latter losing three dollars to $189.00/$193.00.

Dealers said there was no fundamental change in the markets which were still looking for the first exports of the year from Russia to Japan, the leading consumer of the platinum group metals. Deliveries are expected to begin early next month.
"It looks like there is a bit of month-end and half- year buying and borrowing going on in platinum which is making the difference," one dealer said.
